note: Learning profiles. THESE ARE NOT DIAGNOSES AND ARE NEVER STORED AS ONE. A profile is a preset: pick the one that sounds like you, and it configures channels, mission mix, difficulty, coaching strategies and scoring weights all at once. Every setting it applies stays individually changeable afterwards, and 'prefer not to say' is a first-class answer that lands on the widest-compatibility preset. See ADR-0001: the runtime mechanism is channels, not conditions - a profile only chooses a starting point.
principles: A profile changes what the learner DOES, not what the screen is called. If a preset only changed labels it would not be here.
Every preset is reversible from Settings in two actions, from anywhere.
No preset removes a world. Reordering and re-weighting, never removal - deciding somebody cannot learn interviews because of their disability is the exact harm this product exists to refuse.
The learner is never asked to prove or name a condition.

profiles.label: I would rather not say
profiles.easy_read_label: I do not want to say
profiles.blurb: Everything on, nothing assumed. You can change any of it later.

profiles.label: I am Deaf or hard of hearing
profiles.easy_read_label: I do not hear, or I hear a little
profiles.blurb: Captions and sign throughout. Nothing depends on hearing anything.
profiles.notes: Pronunciation is down-weighted to almost nothing rather than removed: a Deaf learner who chooses to use speech should still see their own trend, and a learner who does not never generates the dimension at all. Phone and writing are emphasised because that is where the barrier actually bites.

profiles.label: I do not use speech
profiles.easy_read_label: I do not talk out loud
profiles.blurb: Symbols and typing everywhere. No activity ever requires your voice.
profiles.notes: Session minutes are longer because AAC composition genuinely takes longer - the learner asked for a session length, not a word count, and giving them the same item count would hand them a session twice as long as they asked for.

profiles.label: I stammer
profiles.blurb: Never timed, never scored on fluency. Coaching from real speech therapy strategies.
profiles.notes: Fluency is weighted 0.05, not 0. Removing it entirely would hide a real trend the learner may want to see; weighting it near zero means a bad block week cannot move the composite. Telephone is emphasised because it is the single most avoided situation.

profiles.label: I am blind
profiles.easy_read_label: I do not see the screen
profiles.blurb: Built for a screen reader. Audio-first, and every visual has a spoken equal.
profiles.notes: order_the_steps is down-weighted rather than removed - drag ordering is the hardest mission to make good with a screen reader, so it appears less often and always with a keyboard reorder path.

profiles.label: I have low vision
profiles.blurb: High contrast, large targets, and audio alongside everything.

profiles.label: I am autistic
profiles.blurb: Predictable structure, literal wording, and every social rule stated instead of implied.
profiles.notes: choose_in_context and scenario are up-weighted hard. The gap is rarely vocabulary - it is which of several correct-sounding phrases the room expects, and that is exactly what those two missions drill. Motion reduced by default, changeable.

profiles.label: I learn best with simple words
profiles.easy_read_label: I like easy words and pictures
profiles.blurb: One thing on the screen at a time. Pictures with every idea, and nothing rushed.
profiles.notes: difficulty_ceiling is a pacing choice, not a limit on the learner: the ceiling lifts automatically once a world is mastered, and a trainer can lift it at any time. Sessions are short because a four-minute session finished beats an eight-minute session abandoned.

profiles.label: Reading is hard for me
profiles.blurb: Audio with every piece of text, and never a wall of words.

profiles.label: I have trouble finding words
profiles.blurb: Never rushed, always a symbol to point at, and the word is always offered before it is asked for.
profiles.notes: recognise is weighted highest of any profile. Recognition is reliably preserved when retrieval is not, so a session that opens with recognition opens with a success - and word-finding recovers faster from confidence than from drilling.

profiles.label: I am recovering from a stroke
profiles.easy_read_label: I had a stroke. I am getting better.
profiles.blurb: Short sessions, gentle pace, and progress measured against last week rather than last year.
profiles.notes: Recovery is not linear and a fortnight can go backwards for medical reasons. The baseline window is shortened for this profile so the index tracks the current phase rather than dragging a pre-stroke or early-recovery figure behind it.

profiles.label: I have cerebral palsy
profiles.blurb: Large targets, switch-ready, and nothing anywhere is timed.
profiles.notes: pace weighted 0. Speaking rate in dysarthria is motor function, not skill - see ADR-0006. Switch scanning is on by default for this preset and turned off in one action if the learner does not use one.

profiles.label: Talking at work makes me anxious
profiles.easy_read_label: Talking to people makes me worried
profiles.blurb: Start small, rehearse before it is real, and stop whenever you want.
profiles.notes: roleplay is the most weighted mission here, which looks backwards until you notice the mechanism: avoidance is the maintaining factor in communication anxiety, and graded rehearsal in a place with no consequences is the intervention. Difficulty starts low and every scenario has a visible exit.

easy_onset.label: Easy onset
easy_onset.text: Try starting that word gently, letting the air move before the sound.

light_contact.label: Light contact
light_contact.text: Try touching your lips and tongue lightly on that sound.

pull_out.label: Easing out
pull_out.text: If a sound repeats, try easing out of it slowly rather than pushing through.

pausing.label: Pausing
pausing.text: A silent pause works just as well as a filler word, and sounds confident.

breath_support.label: Breath
breath_support.text: Try taking a breath before you start, and letting the sentence ride out on it.

voluntary_disclosure.label: Saying it first
voluntary_disclosure.text: Some people find it easier to say 'I stammer, so give me a second' at the start. It is your choice, and it often relaxes the room.

ask_to_face_me.label: Ask them to face you
ask_to_face_me.text: Try: "Could you face me when you speak? It helps me follow."

ask_in_writing.label: Ask for it in writing
ask_in_writing.text: Try: "Could you send me that in a message?"

seat_yourself_to_see.label: Where you sit
seat_yourself_to_see.text: In a meeting, a seat where you can see everyone's face does more than any technology.

confirm_back.label: Say it back
confirm_back.text: Repeat the instruction in your own words. It catches problems before they cost anything.

compose_ahead.label: Write it before
compose_ahead.text: You can build your answer before the conversation starts. Nobody is waiting.

phrase_bank_shortcut.label: Keep it ready
phrase_bank_shortcut.text: Save the phrases you use most. Fast to reach beats perfect to build.

ask_for_response_time.label: Ask them to wait
ask_for_response_time.text: Try: "Give me a moment - I am putting it together."

written_introduction.label: Introduce yourself once
written_introduction.text: A short saved introduction saves explaining yourself every single time.

state_your_name_first.label: Name first
state_your_name_first.text: Saying "It's Ravi" before you speak saves everyone guessing.

ask_who_is_here.label: Who is in the room
ask_who_is_here.text: Try: "Could we go round and say who's here?"

request_verbal_agenda.label: Ask what is coming
request_verbal_agenda.text: Try: "Could you tell me what we're covering?"

ask_for_larger_print.label: Ask for bigger
ask_for_larger_print.text: Try: "Could I have that in a larger size?"

ask_to_read_it_aloud.label: Ask them to read it
ask_to_read_it_aloud.text: Try: "Could you read that out for me?"

request_good_lighting.label: Ask about the light
request_good_lighting.text: Where you stand and where the light falls changes what you can see. It is fine to ask.

say_what_you_mean.label: Say it straight
say_what_you_mean.text: Direct is not rude. "I need this by Friday" is clearer and kinder than hinting.

ask_for_the_rule.label: Ask what the rule is
ask_for_the_rule.text: Try: "What's the usual way this is done here?" Most rules are unwritten, and asking is allowed.

script_the_opening.label: Plan the first line
script_the_opening.text: Having the first sentence ready carries you into the rest of it.

name_the_ambiguity.label: Name the fog
name_the_ambiguity.text: Try: "I'm not sure if you mean today or this week - which is it?"

agree_a_signal.label: Agree a signal
agree_a_signal.text: Agreeing a sign with one colleague for "I need a minute" costs nothing and helps a lot.

one_thing_at_a_time.label: One thing
one_thing_at_a_time.text: Do the first step. Then the next. You do not need to hold all of it at once.

ask_for_a_picture.label: Ask for a picture
ask_for_a_picture.text: Try: "Could you show me?" Seeing it once beats hearing it three times.

repeat_it_back.label: Say it back
repeat_it_back.text: Saying it back in your words makes it stick, and shows you have it.

ask_someone_to_show_me.label: Ask to be shown
ask_someone_to_show_me.text: Try: "Could you show me once?" That is a normal thing to ask on any job.

ask_for_extra_reading_time.label: Ask for time to read
ask_for_extra_reading_time.text: Try: "Give me a minute with this and I'll come back to you."

use_a_template.label: Start from a template
use_a_template.text: A saved shape for emails removes the hardest part, which is the blank page.

check_it_back.label: Read it once more
check_it_back.text: One pass before you send catches most of it.

point_to_it.label: Point
point_to_it.text: Pointing is communicating. It is not a lesser way of saying it.

describe_around_it.label: Go round the word
describe_around_it.text: If the word will not come, describe it. "The thing for cutting" gets you there.

ask_for_a_choice.label: Ask for choices
ask_for_a_choice.text: Try: "Give me two options and I'll pick." Choosing is easier than finding.

write_the_first_letter.label: First letter
write_the_first_letter.text: Writing or tracing the first letter often unlocks the whole word.

take_the_time_you_need.label: Your own time
take_the_time_you_need.text: There is no clock here. There never will be.

ask_someone_to_wait.label: Ask them to hold on
ask_someone_to_wait.text: Try: "One moment." Two words buy you all the time you need.

rest_and_return.label: Stop and come back
rest_and_return.text: Stopping halfway is not failing. Your progress is saved exactly where you left it.

rehearse_it_first.label: Practise it here first
rehearse_it_first.text: Say it here, where nothing depends on it, before you say it there.

start_with_one_person.label: One person first
start_with_one_person.text: One colleague is easier than a room. Start there and let it grow.

you_can_stop_anytime.label: You can stop
you_can_stop_anytime.text: You can leave any activity at any point, and nothing is lost or marked.
